Open-source AI is undercutting Big AI's margins.

Even amid the rapid scale of AI, open-source models cost far less per token, the basic unit of AI computing.

For example, Anthropic’s Fable 5 model was more than 50 times more expensive per token than DeepSeek’s V4 Pro.

Other open-source models from Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and Nvidia are also competing at a fraction of the cost of leading proprietary models.

As cheaper alternatives improve, proprietary AI companies will face increasing pressure to lower prices.

This could potentially squeeze profit margins all as CapEx is surging.

Keep watching open-source AI.

On agents:

Dealing with real estate agents is like dealing with brokers in listed equities. Don't even ask their opinion. You need to do your own homework. 

Talk to other owners in the area. This is something I always do. 

With stocks, charts are my go to source. 

Have a plan. Read. Investigate. Fish for crucial information when dealing with agents. I.e. how long has the property been listed? What was the last offer? How many owners on the title deed (more owners more difficulty in agreement)? Is it a seller or buyer market? What is going on with yields? Are banks easy on lending?

In real estate there is an interesting starting calculation. Yield. After costs (taxes, renovation/management fees etc.) how much money the property makes and in how many years you can recover it. 4-5% yield after costs is considered good investment. 6-8% yield is great.

I see this calculation very similar to the initial stop-loss and risk/reward measurement. You look at a breakout opportunity and it has 1:2.5 risk/reward. You say its not very lucrative. But the stock is breaking out to new all-time highs. As you immediately raise your stop after take off, and price exceeds the pattern objective, the risk/reward starts looking like 1:10. 

Real estate appreciates in value + rentals depending on the scarcity/inflation move higher in time. So the initial calculation ends up changing a lot. It is never static calculation.

The global debt crisis is set to get even worse:

The US fiscal deficit is projected to widen to -6.1% of GDP in 2027, its largest since 2012, excluding the pandemic years of 2020 and 2021.

This will be the biggest deficit as a % of GDP among the 5 major developed economies, including the UK, Germany, France, and Japan.

Furthermore, Germany's deficit is expected to widen from -2.7% of GDP in 2025 to -4.1% in 2027, its largest since 2010, excluding the 2020 pandemic.

Japan's fiscal deficit is estimated to more than triple, from -0.7% to -2.5% of GDP, its largest since 2022.

The UK is the only economy expected to improve its fiscal position, with its deficit narrowing from -4.3% in 2025, to -3.1% of GDP next year, while France's budget gap is projected to widen to -5.2%.

Deficit spending is only accelerating.
